one_month_reasoning: FQ1 FY27 (quarter ended 2026-10-02) results and FQ2 guide are very likely inside the window: no date announced yet, but precedents are 2023-10-26, 2024-10-22 and 2025-10-28 (~90% before Nov 1). Guide is $4.1B +/- $0.1B and $7.30 +/- $0.20. Chain evidence points to a beat: street $/TB rose 15-92% Mar-Aug 2026 with nothing falling (eRacks), WD guided 55-56% GM, and pricing for all of CY2027 is already contracted. But the stock will trade on the CY2028 pricing / Toshiba answer, and the July print was two-sided (-8.5% on the day, then recovered). WDC and hyperscaler capex prints also land in late Oct. Net: median ~$842 (+0.5%), sigma ~19.5% monthly (slightly under 75%/3.5 because the earnings event is the main swing and fundamentals are strong), roughly symmetric; essentially unchanged from round 1.

reasoning: Round 2. Supervisor corrections adopted: diluted shares ~230M (exchangeables settled 2026-09-08, no further dilution), gross debt ~$2.4B, the FY28 'consensus' $55.37 is a single unverified secondary source, nearline volume is allocated into 2028 but pricing is set only for CY2027, and the Q1x4 'mid-cycle' leg ignores guided sequential growth. I rebuilt EPS bottom-up: FY27 ~$33-34, FY28 ~$47 on 230M shares. In-lane checks: Toshiba remains MAMR-only in mass production until 2H FY2028 (Feb 2026 roadmap), it held ~11% of nearline exabytes in 2024 (TrendFocus) after its 2022 doubling plan, and street $/TB rose 15-92% Mar-Aug 2026 with no declines (eRacks), with Toshiba's own MG line +38%. So the Toshiba plan is a CY2028 pricing/multiple risk rather than an FY27 earnings risk; I quantify it at roughly +3-6% industry EB by end-CY2027 against mid-20s % demand growth, which I agree with. Note mreport cites Toshiba at ~17% of HDD units, so its exabyte share is lower than unit share; the '30% target' is Nikkei-only. Fair value rises to ~$790 (P/E $799, FCF $850, flat-pricing $608 at 15%) from $780; scenario mean ~$886. I keep a lognormal-like ladder with median ~$840 and sigma ~0.58, with a slightly fat left tail for the cycle base rate, giving P(>=838)=0.50 (from 0.49). Research was limited to ~4 web searches/fetches this round.
